name: Di Fu
bio: Dr Di Fu is an Assistant Professor in the School of Psychology and an Interdisciplinary Principal Fellow at the Surrey Institute for People-Centred AI (PAI), University of Surrey. She directs the Social Interaction and Embodied Intelligence (SEIL) Lab. She investigates how social cues guide attention, how people integrate information across senses, and how they interact and cooperate with robots and AI systems. Her work connects cognitive experiments and computational modelling with studies of embodied robots, voice assistants and conversational agents, using artificial systems both to investigate human social mechanisms and to explore human-grounded AI.
background: She received her PhD in Cognitive Neuroscience from the Institute of Psychology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, in 2020, and undertook a joint PhD programme at the University of Hamburg from 2017 to 2020. Before joining Surrey, she was a Postdoctoral Research Associate in Hamburg’s Department of Informatics, working on the Crossmodal Learning project from 2020 to 2023.
